summary: The proposal presents a well-motivated and clearly structured research topic (LLM-powered thesis review feedback), but it has a critical bibliography shortfall (only 5 of the required minimum 6 references) and several major issues that must be resolved before submission: schedule dates are internally inconsistent with the stated thesis period, multiple iteration deliverables lack measurable outcomes, the AI transparency statement omits required section-level detail, and the core system component is named inconsistently across sections. Writing style also shows recurring violations (forbidden sentence starters, passive voice) and minor formatting/paragraph-structure deviations that should be cleaned up.

findings.title: Bibliography contains only 5 publications; minimum of 6 required
findings.description: The bibliography lists only 5 entries ([TP21], [AAM17], [BBE10], [Bog+07], [NM06]). The guidelines require at least 6–8 peer-reviewed publications. The student must add at least one additional relevant peer-reviewed publication to meet the minimum threshold.

locations.quote: [TP21] T. Tuononen and A. Parpala … [AAM17] P. Ashwin, A. Abbas, and M. McLean … [BBE10] J. Bitchener, H. Basturkmen, and M. East … [Bog+07] M. Bogo, C. Regehr, R. Power, and G. Regehr … [NM06] D. J. Nicol and D. Macfarlane-Dick …

findings.title: Iteration dates inconsistent with thesis start date and total duration
findings.description: The thesis is stated to start on 26.06.2026 and end on 26.10.2026 (~17.4 weeks), yet Iteration 1 begins on 08.06.2026, which is 18 days before the stated start date. Furthermore, the nine iterations span 08.06–26.10, totaling approximately 20 weeks of work, which exceeds the actual 17.4-week thesis period. The dates need to be reconciled so all iterations fall within the declared start–end window and the total planned work fits within the available time.

locations.quote: The Bachelor thesis starts on 26.06.2026 and the submission is on 26.10.2026.
Iteration 1 (08.06.2026 - 2 weeks)
Iteration 9 (05.10.2026 - 3 weeks)

findings.title: Vague, non-measurable deliverables in several iterations
findings.description: Several iterations contain tasks that lack concrete, measurable outcomes. 'Modularize Thesis Management to prepare integration' (Iter 1) does not state what the modularized structure looks like or what the acceptance criterion is. 'Build prototype implementations for agentic and prompt chaining setups' and 'Evaluate agentic and prompt chaining setups' (Iter 5) do not specify what the prototype must demonstrate or what evaluation metrics will be used. 'Build prototype implementations for the selected LLM models and providers' and 'Evaluate different LLM models and providers' (Iter 6) are similarly underspecified. 'Review the system and check for bugs' (Iter 9) is not a measurable deliverable. Each task should state a specific, verifiable outcome.

findings.title: AI transparency statement does not specify which sections the tools were used for
findings.description: The statement says tools were used 'across different stages of the writing process' but never names specific proposal sections (e.g., Abstract, Introduction, Problem, Motivation, Objective, Schedule). The guidelines require the statement to specify which sections the AI tools were applied to. The student should indicate, for example, which tools were used in which sections.

locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across diferent stages of the writing process.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming: "Reviewer" vs "feedback tool"
findings.description: The same system component is called an "LLM-powered Reviewer" (or "LLM Reviewer" / "This Reviewer") in the Motivation section and its figure caption, but is then referred to as "the feedback tool" throughout the Objective section and Figure 2 caption. The two names are never reconciled, leaving the reader uncertain whether they denote the same entity or different components. The author should pick one term (or explicitly define the relationship) and use it consistently.

locations.quote: an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group's writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback
an LLM Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, generating formative feedback on the thesis
When the feedback tool has access to previous iterations of the proposal or thesis, it can compare the latest submission with earlier ones
the supervisor and the feedback tool work in parallel, with specialized agents analyzing the thesis
supervisors invoke the feedback tool to write feedback directly into Thesis Management

findings.title: Forbidden sentence starters: 'As', 'Since', and 'Because'
findings.description: Three sentences begin with forbidden sentence starters ('As', 'Since', 'Because') per the group's writing style guidelines. Each should be restructured: (1) 'As Figure 1 illustrates…' → 'Figure 1 illustrates…'; (2) 'Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format…' → 'Guidelines may not already be in a suitable format; in that case…'; (3) 'Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs…' → 'The feedback tool is powered by LLMs, so…'.

locations.quote: As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group's writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback [NM06].
Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on.
Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.

findings.title: Documentation task included in the schedule
findings.description: Iteration 9 lists 'Documentation' as a work item. The schedule should focus exclusively on development and research deliverables; thesis writing and documentation tasks should not appear here. If documentation is needed, it should be removed from the iteration plan.

locations.quote: Iteration 9 (05.10.2026 - 3 weeks) • Review the system and check for bugs • Documentation

findings.title: Passive voice in two instances
findings.description: Two phrases use passive voice where active voice with an identifiable actor is required: (1) 'are governed by institutional conventions' → 'institutional conventions rather than research substance govern these issues'; (2) 'no LLM-generated feedback is produced at all' → 'the tool produces no LLM-generated feedback, and all feedback comes from the supervisor.'

locations.quote: Having to wait for feedback on purely formal aspects of a thesis or proposal can be frustrating for students, as these issues are governed by institutional conventions rather than research substance.
In one mode, no LLM-generated feedback is produced at all and all feedback comes from the supervisor.

findings.title: Objectives presented as a numbered list instead of a bullet list
findings.description: The guidelines specify that the Objective section must start with a short introduction and a bullet list of 3-4 high-level objectives. The proposal uses a numbered list (1., 2., 3., 4.) instead of an unordered/bullet list. Change the numbered items to bullet points to match the guideline.

locations.quote: The scope of the thesis is to fulfill the following goals: 1. Generate Feedback Based on Guidelines 2. Highlight Changes Across Iterations 3. Compare Prompting Techniques and LLM Models 4. Integrate With Thesis Management

findings.title: Single-line paragraph at end of Introduction
findings.description: The sentence 'The student, by contrast, hands in the thesis itself as a single final submission.' stands alone as a one-line paragraph at the end of Section 1. Paragraphs should be 5–8 lines; this 1-line paragraph should be merged into the preceding paragraph about the iterative proposal workflow.

locations.quote: The student, by contrast, hands in the thesis itself as a single final submission.

findings.title: Paragraph exceeds 10 lines in Motivation
findings.description: The paragraph beginning 'Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors…' spans approximately 11 rendered lines, exceeding the 10-line upper bound. It can be split after the sentence ending '[BBE10, NM06]' to separate the description of the Reviewer's role from the resulting benefits.

locations.quote: Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors with non-content-related feedback could improve the thesis writing process. As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor…

findings.title: Paragraph exceeds 10 lines and mixes multiple ideas in Motivation
findings.description: The paragraph beginning 'Better and faster feedback has significant advantages for students as well…' spans approximately 12 rendered lines (continuing from page 4 onto page 5) and covers at least three distinct ideas: (1) the immediacy benefit of faster feedback, (2) the student's knowledge-and-beliefs model and self-regulated learning process, and (3) the LLM-powered capability to obtain instant feedback at any point. It should be split into at least two paragraphs.

locations.quote: Better and faster feedback has significant advantages for students as well. When feedback arrives sooner, students can act on it while the writing process is still fresh in their minds. The student brings both knowledge… Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.

findings.title: Inconsistent hyphenation: "prompt-chaining" vs "prompt chaining"
findings.description: The technique is written with a hyphen on page 2 ("prompt-chaining") but without a hyphen on pages 8 and 9 ("prompt chaining") in both noun and modifier positions. Pick one form and use it consistently throughout the proposal.

findings.title: Introductory text says 'two-week iterations' but Iterations 8 and 9 are three weeks
findings.description: The schedule introduction states 'We divided the time into several two-week iterations,' yet Iteration 8 and Iteration 9 are each listed as 3 weeks. The descriptive text should be updated to reflect the actual iteration lengths (e.g., 'two- to three-week iterations').
